slides.title: VibeAct: Vibration to Actions for Contact-Rich Reactive Robot Dexterity
slides.highlight: VibeAct uses piezoelectric microphones and a shared physical representation of contact and slip to bridge real vibrotactile sensing with simulation-based reinforcement learning. This approach enables robot hands to perform contact-rich tasks like regrasping and insertion by utilizing rapid tactile feedback.

card.one_liner: VibeAct enables sim-to-real dexterous manipulation by bridging vibrotactile sensing and RL via a shared contact-slip representation.
card.key_idea: A tactile estimator maps real piezoelectric microphone signals to a low-dimensional contact/slip representation, which is also used to train RL policies in simulation.
card.evaluation: Tested on five contact-rich tasks (e.g., peg insertion) using PPO; outperformed proprioception+point-cloud baselines in simulation and improved real-world success rates.
card.limitation: Discards raw signal details (texture, location), requires accurate object pose tracking for labeling, and is tied to specific hardware configurations.

slides.title: Self Capacitive Tactile Sensor System designed for Companion Robots
slides.tldr: SCALABLE TACTILE SENSING FOR COMPANION ROBOTS
slides.highlight: This work presents a scalable self-capacitance tactile sensing system using conductive fabric, enabling real-time interaction detection for companion robots. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A scalable, FPGA-based self-capacitive tactile sensing system designed for the companion robot HIRO-chan.
card.key_idea: Uses a single conductive fabric layer and RC relaxation sensing, with a decision-tree classifier implemented on an FPGA to offload real-time inference from the main processor.
card.evaluation: Tested a 100-point array at 10, 100, and 1000 Hz; 100 Hz reliably classified five interaction types with 90.4% accuracy.
card.limitation: Currently limited to 100 sensors and a small set of interaction gestures, insufficient for full-body coverage.

slides.title: Bridging Handheld and Teleoperated Supervision for Contact-Rich Manipulation via State-Gated Experts
slides.tldr: HYBRID DATA STRATEGY FOR CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: The BRIDGE framework combines scalable handheld data with targeted teleoperated demonstrations using a mixture of diffusion policy experts to improve success rates in contact-sensitive tasks.

card.one_liner: BRIDGE improves contact-rich manipulation by routing between handheld-observed and teleoperated-desired action experts based on robot state.
card.key_idea: A mixture-of-diffusion-experts architecture that uses a state-conditioned MLP router to switch between a base policy (observed actions) and a support head (desired actions).
card.evaluation: Tested on three contact-rich tasks (pulley routing, pipe insertion, battery insertion) against handheld and teleoperated baselines; success rates improved by up to 36.7%.
card.limitation: Hard-switching causes control discontinuities; identifying support phases is currently empirical; may scale poorly to long-horizon tasks with many contact regimes.

slides.title: NoContactNoWorries: Estimating Contact through Vision and Proprioception for In-Hand Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work presents a multimodal framework that fuses RGB-D vision and proprioception to infer binary contact states, contributing to the multimodal social perception goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: A transformer-based framework that predicts binary fingertip contact using only RGB-D vision and robot proprioception.
card.key_idea: Fuses RGB-D tokens with current and commanded joint configurations via pose-conditioned cross-attention and a causal transformer to capture spatiotemporal contact dynamics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via F1 scores and in-hand reorientation tasks on simulated and real LEAP hands across seen and novel objects; results show robust generalization.
card.limitation: Performance degrades on real hardware due to sensing noise and visual ambiguity, especially with highly occluded, non-convex object geometries.

slides.title: PhysReflect-VLA: Physical Feasibility and Self-Reflective Regulation for Reliable Vision-Language-Action Policies
slides.tldr: SELF-REFLECTIVE VLA FRAMEWORK FOR ROBOTIC MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a framework that uses a reflection module and feasibility operators to diagnose execution errors and generate corrective guidance, aligning with ADAM-CHAT's focus on self-monitoring and self-correction.

card.one_liner: PhysReflect-VLA enhances VLA policies with real-time physical feasibility checks and self-reflective error correction.
card.key_idea: A plug-and-play framework using a bidirectional consistency model (forward/inverse operators) to filter infeasible actions and an LLM-based module to generate corrective guidance from execution discrepancies.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five real-world robotic manipulation tasks against baselines like OpenVLA; achieved an average success rate gain of 5.4%.

slides.title: LIBERO-Safety: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Physical and Semantic Safety in Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.highlight: This work introduces a parametric safety benchmark and a large-scale dataset to evaluate physical and semantic safety in Vision-Language-Action models, contributing to the development of reliable embodied AI for RwB.

card.one_liner: LIBERO-Safety is a comprehensive benchmark evaluating physical and semantic safety in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.
card.key_idea: A parametric benchmark using UBDDL for procedural scene generation and a keypose-driven pipeline to synthesize 19,664 collision-free demonstrations via an optimization-based motion planner.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 8 VLA and 2 foundation models across 75 tasks using Success Rate, Collision Rate, and Refusal Rate; results show critical OOD vulnerabilities.
card.limitation: Task success is bottlenecked by sub-optimal trajectory synthesis and semantic misalignment, even when physical safety constraints are maintained.

slides.title: Learning to Fold: prizewinning solution at LeHome Challenge 2026
slides.tldr: BIMANUAL GARMENT FOLDING VIA VLA AND RL
slides.highlight: This work presents a vision-language-action (VLA) policy enhanced by a reinforcement-learning loop for bimanual garment folding, achieving top rankings in both simulation and real-world settings.

card.one_liner: A bimanual garment-folding VLA policy improved via RL, placing 1st online and 2nd offline in LeHome 2026.
card.key_idea: Combines AWR and RECAP-style advantage conditioning with a VLA that acts as its own value function via auxiliary prediction heads.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 4 garment types in Isaac Sim (online) and physical robots (offline) using geometric keypoint-distance success criteria.
card.limitation: The system was built iteratively under competition pressure with few formal ablations, making specific component necessity unclear.

slides.title: Stage-Aware and Roughness-Constrained Diffusion Policy for Multi-Stage Robotic Polishing
slides.tldr: STAGE-AWARE DIFFUSION POLICY FOR ROBOTIC POLISHING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a diffusion policy that infers process stages from multimodal observation histories to ensure consistent action generation. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and state recognition within hybrid systems.

card.one_liner: A diffusion-based policy for robotic polishing that ensures stage-consistency and surface roughness quality constraints.
card.key_idea: Combines a stage-inference network for conditioned reverse denoising with a roughness-oriented process model to guide diffusion sampling of feed speed and contact force.
card.evaluation: Validated via real-robot experiments on spacecraft cabin coating and inner-cavity finishing, comparing against advanced baselines and using ablation studies.
